subject: management-of-business
title: Inventory Control: The Sawtooth Stock Chart

questions.prompt: A storekeeper says: Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The storekeeper is right - ordering earlier wastes money on stock that is not needed yet

Reorder when falling stock reaches the reorder level, not when it runs out: deliveries take a lead time to arrive, during which stock keeps falling, and the reorder level is set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage precisely so stock bottoms out at the buffer - never below it - just as the delivery lands.
Reorder when stock reaches the buffer stock of 250 units, because the buffer is the trigger line
Reorder every Monday regardless of the stock level

questions.misconception: Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away. In fact Reorder when falling stock reaches the reorder level, not when it runs out: deliveries take a lead time to arrive, during which stock keeps falling, and the reorder level is set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage precisely so stock bottoms out at the buffer - never below it - just as the delivery lands.

questions.prompt: Stock starts at 1,000 units and usage is steady at 125 units a day. On which day does stock reach the reorder level of 500 units?
questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: stock must fall 500 units at 125 units a day, and 500 / 125 = 4, so the reorder level is reached on day 4.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state how the reorder level of 500 units is calculated from the buffer stock and the lead time.
questions.answer: Reorder level = buffer stock 250 units + lead-time usage (2 days x 125 units a day = 250 units) = 500 units.
questions.explanation: The deciding habit is to build the reorder level from its two parts: the buffer floor plus the stock that will be used while the delivery is on its way.

questions.prompt: An order is placed on day 4 and the lead time is 2 days. State the day the delivery arrives and the stock level at that moment, and explain why.
questions.answer: The delivery arrives on day 6, when stock has fallen a further 2 x 125 = 250 units from 500 to the buffer stock of 250 units - it bottoms out at the buffer, never below it, just as the delivery lands.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows the lead-time fall directly: stock keeps being used while the order is in transit, and the buffer is the floor it reaches.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the sawtooth cycle in order?

choices.text: Fall at the usage rate, reorder at 500 units, wait through the 2-day lead time, delivery lands, stock jumps back to 1,000 units
Delivery lands, stock jumps, reorder at zero, wait, stock falls
Fall to zero, reorder, delivery arrives straight away, stock jumps
Stock stays at the maximum level, then falls once to the buffer and stops

questions.explanation: Scene 4 names the repeating cycle: fall, reorder, wait, delivery, jump - and then the same tooth repeats.
